full_name: Club de Golf Costa Brava (Red Course)

summary.text: Club de Golf Costa Brava at Santa Cristina d'Aro is one of the first golf clubs on the Costa Brava; its first 18 holes, by John Hamilton Stutt, opened in 1968.

setting.text: The club says the Red Course has more water than the Green, with undulating, fast greens that test the short game.
The club says its five par fives make the Red Course a challenge for power hitters.
The Green Course's back nine, which forms part of the Red, is flatter and approaches the Vall d'Aro, according to the club.
Where2golf calls the course not overly hilly or long but tight in places, on tree-lined fairways of pine and cork oak past luxury villas.
The club says it uses recycled water for irrigation and electric vehicles.

history.text: The Masia that became the clubhouse was built in 1841.
Club de Golf Costa Brava was founded on 10 April 1962.
The first 18 holes opened in 1968, designed by John Hamilton Stutt, whom the club credits with Turnberry and St Mellion Old.
The club says the opening coincided with the social boom around S'Agaro and Platja d'Aro, drawing film stars including Sean Connery, who played the new course.
Nine new holes were added in 2011, making 27 in all, designed by Jorge Soler and Eugenio Aguado, according to the club.
The Red Course combines the back nine of the Green Course with the holes added in 2011, according to the club.
About 300 people attended the 50th anniversary event on 11 August 2018.
Top100golfcourses says the club was founded in 1962 but the course did not appear for another six years.

trivia.text: The Red Course is a par 73 with five par 5s, a test for big hitters, according to the club.
The club calls itself the oldest and only social golf club on the Costa Brava.
The club's other 18, the Green Course, is par 70 and unusual for having six par threes, according to the club.

1.text: A par four listed at 365 metres with a pronounced dogleg left that limits the driver, and a large pine left of the fairway.

2.text: A par five listed at 455 metres, doglegging left to right with forest down the right. The club calls it a birdie opportunity.

3.text: A long par three listed at 205 metres needing a long iron or a wood, with two bunkers around a flat green.

5.text: The club says it is the longest par five on the course, at 508 metres, with out of bounds left and a huge pine in the middle of the fairway.

6.text: A straight, level par three listed at 173 metres, with a lake on the right.

7.text: A par four listed at 383 metres that the club describes as stroke index 1, a dogleg left with a stream to avoid off the tee.

8.text: A par four listed at 317 metres with two water hazards off the tee and a complex green with three platforms.

9.text: A par five listed at 482 metres with a stream to cross on the second shot and a large lake left of the green.

11.text: A short par four listed at 289 metres that the club calls a challenge filled with water, ending at a slightly elevated island green.

15.text: A par five listed at 459 metres, with a large oak tree about 100 metres from the green.

17.text: A short par three listed at 134 metres, where a stream winds around the right of the green and behind it.

18.text: A par four listed at 380 metres with a century-old olive tree as a tee-shot marker, a stream down the left, and a green split into two platforms.
The clubhouse terrace has views of the 18th hole.

local.text: The club is on the Costa Brava at Santa Cristina d'Aro, in the Girona area.
Where2golf puts it about 30 km south-east of Girona.
The club's villa-lined surroundings include S'Agaro and Platja d'Aro, per the club's history page.
The clubhouse is a Catalan farmhouse the club dates to 1841, flanked by two cypress trees.
